NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City Council of the City of St. Petersburg, Florida, that (I) the Community Development Block Grant -Disaster Recovery Agreement between the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”), Pinellas County, Florida (“County”) and the City of St. Petersburg, Florida (“ City”) related to a geo-coding error that resulted in $173,681,000 in CDBG-DR funds that should have been part of the City’s federal award being included in the County’s federal award (“Misallocated Funds”) and (ii) the CDBG -DR Funds Coordination Agreement between the County and the City that establishes a coordinated and efficient framework for the use and oversight of the misallocated funds are hereby approved.

EXPLANATION: Congress appropriated funds through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) Community Development Block Grant - Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) Program in response to the 2023 Hurricane Idalia (DR-4734-FL) and the 2024 Hurricane Helene (DR-4828- FL). Assistance for these disasters was appropriated on December 21, 2024, by the Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act of 2025. The City of St. Petersburg (City) was allocated $159,884,000 per the Allocation Announcement Notice (90 FR 4759) published on January 16, 2025. On June 12, 2025, City Council approved the CDBG-DR Action Plan for the use of the federal grant funds (Resolution No. 2025-327) which allocated $6,000,000 to the Non-Profit Community Support Services (NPCSS) program. HUD approved the City’s Action Plan in August 2025 and executed the City’s Grant Agreement in February 2026. Through extensive public input and Unmet Needs and Mitigation Needs Assessments in the Action Plan, the City determined the need to create the Non-Profit Community Support Services (NPCSS) program to address the increased need for essential community services as a result of the qualifying disasters.
